subject: PeakAI renewal: sizing runway & surge-proofing proposal
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara@peakai.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal sizing — sudden spike last month, need plan

Hi Nikhil,

Quick note from our ops team: during an ad-hoc product test two weeks ago we saw a 3x burst in gen requests for a ~6 hour window. Our average utilization is within what we contracted, but the tail behavior pushed queueing and increased 95th-pct latency above our SLAs for ~20 minutes.

We start renewal talks next month and want to ensure committed capacity covers these spikes without resorting to high-cost burst credits every time. Can you outline options for: 1) staged top-up commitments, 2) a surge reserve pattern, and 3) any telemetry or alerting we should enable to avoid surprises?

Attached is our quick usage export (peakai-usage-summary-2026q1.csv). Happy to hop on a 30m call — Sara and our lead infra engineer (ops@peakai.com) can join.

Thanks,
Sara Lopez
VP, Platform
PeakAI

---
Attachments: peakai-usage-summary-2026q1.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@peakai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal sizing — sudden spike last month, need plan

Sara — thanks for the data and flag. We dug into the export you attached and pulled a short diagnostic. High-level takeaways:

- The 6-hour window had a concentrated window of short-sequence gen calls (avg length ~40 tokens) with a high concurrency burst (sustained 300 concurrent requests) driven by one campaign.
- KV-cache hit-rate dropped ~18% during the burst, which increased per-token cost and latency due to cache warm-ups and repeated attention passes.
- Batching efficiency fell from ~1.8 tokens/request to ~0.6 during the spike because requests were short and skewed in arrival times.

Options we recommend (details below):
1) Hybrid reserve: keep your current committed slab and add a small dedicated surge reserve (4 H100-equivalent slots) that auto-attaches during periods where 95th-pct concurrency > 240 for > 10m.
2) Staged commit top-ups: convert two months of burst history into a staggered tranche — +8 H100 equivalent over 3 quarters, with staged billing so it’s capex-light.
3) Telemetry & preflight: enable the 95th-pct concurrency alert + KV cache warm-up metric; we’ll send a Playbook for experiments that reduces cache thrash.

I can get Ben to sketch the cost/latency tradeoffs and Kimberly to propose the exact alert thresholds and rollout.

Propose a short call tomorrow 10:30am PT to review — does that work?

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Referenced attachments: peakai-usage-summary-2026q1.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: PeakAI sizing scenarios + recommended commit mix

(Internal only)

Quick note following Nikhil's summary. I modeled three scenarios using our kernel-selection cost model and the workload shape from the CSV:

Scenario A — Conservative: +4 H100-equivalent surge reserve (on-call attach)
- Expected 95th-pct latency reduction: ~22% during bursts
- Cost impact (annualized): +12% on current committed spend
- Pros: minimal billing friction; preserves current reserve commitments
- Cons: may still require manual tranche top-ups if bursts lengthen

Scenario B — Staged Commit: +8 H100-equivalent phased over 3 quarters (2/quarter)
- Latency improvements similar to A but more reliable throughput for extended campaigns
- Cost impact: +28% annualized but smoother billing via tranche staging
- Pros: predictable performance, reduces burst credits use to near-zero
- Cons: longer contract amendments required

Scenario C — Smart-tier routing + small commit: +3 H100-equivalent + routing rule (route low-latency requests to cheaper variants during non-burst)
- Best cost/latency balance for irregular bursts
- Requires config changes and a short validation window (2–3 weeks)

Recommendations: lead with Scenario B as the default for renewal conversations (customer values predictability) and offer Scenario C as an optics-friendly cost-saving add-on. For the short-term immediate mitigation we can propose Scenario A as a safety net.

Action items for Kimberly: can you draft alert thresholds and the KV cache warm-up runbook? I’ll prepare the pricing slides and an amortized cost table for the renewal.

-Ben
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments suggested: proposed-commit-scenarios.xlsx (will include amortized cost table)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara@peakai.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal sizing — sudden spike last month, need plan

Sara — thanks for flagging and for the data. Follow-up from our internal review and proposed next steps: 

1) Immediate mitigation (troubleshooting window)
- We recommend enabling the 95th-percentile concurrency alert at 220 concurrent requests (5-min evaluation) and an automated attach of the 4-slot surge reserve when it fires. This will buy you breathing room while we validate patterns.

2) Renewal recommendation (preferred)
- Staged Commit (8 H100-equivalent over 3 quarters) with a 30% rollback window for the first 60 days post-rollout. This gives runway for PeakAI’s campaigns without large upfront increases.

3) Observability & runbook
- Enable KV cache miss-rate dashboard (existing Redwood metric) and a short experiment: if miss-rate > 12% during a burst, enable aggressive prefix caching for 48 hours.

4) Paperwork and timeline
- Nikhil: propose we present Scenario B with Scenario C as a cost-saving optional appendix in the renewal packet. Ben — can you include the amortized cost table and a small one-time credit (2% of incremental commit) to help bridge procurement?

If that all sounds ok we’ll draft the renewal amendment and the onboarding runbook. I’ll also add the HubSpot link and a DocuSign stub to the packet.

Thanks — available for the call tomorrow 10:30am PT (Nikhil requested).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success — Renewals
Redwood Inference
